correctness.rationale: For N>=3, Vandermonde determinant gives a.s. rank. The normalized (z-Z1)^(N-1) coefficient vector and exact cluster event give P(Lambda<=s)>=c s^((m-1)/(2N-2)), which forces mean inverse divergence through m=2N-1. Lagrange numerator norms are bounded by sqrt(binomial(2N-2,N-1)); conditional reciprocal chords are stochastically bounded by independent exponentials after logarithms. Exact gamma tails yield the square-block estimate. Positive-Gram superadditivity across k disjoint independent blocks gives P(Lambda<=s)<=C s^(k/2)log(1/s)^(k(N-2)); layer-cake proves p<k/2, and trace inverse<=N/Lambda proves m>=3N finite. Tested accompanying CHECK.py with 5715 assertions; finite tests are supplementary.

value.rationale: The mathematical gap is not merely a small constant improvement: the motivating 2026 paper asserts infinite expected noise risk for all independent uniform Fourier sampling counts. An all-N counter-regime with demonstrably finite mean risk distinguishes row collisions from genuine loss of column rank, and a matching all-cluster obstruction below 2N gives a natural, dimension-scaled partial phase diagram. This remains meaningful despite the sufficient 3N threshold being nonsharp and despite elementary block combining of a known square tail. The paper provides an explicit correction target for finite-noise sampling design.
